fieldValues.title: A change to a cross-cutting rule left copies of the rule behind, and each surfaced only when the next link ran
fieldValues.summary: srs-rust#1473 routed the definition writers in package_service through one versioned filename rule. Driving semanticops.com#42 then hit, one link at a time: srs-rust#1512 (a name lookup that ignored version), srs-rust#1513 (repository_portability had its own unversioned copy of the rule, ten sites, so .srsj lost every version but the last), and srs-web bindings still at build.554 (a single-file .srsj could not hold two versions). Each cost a build, a review and a release cycle.
evidence: srs-web branch 617-link-proposals: bindings advanced to build.575
fieldValues.body:
- What would have caught it: before closing a change to a rule, search every copy of the rule (here: format strings building definition paths, and every by-name type lookup) and every consumer that pins the old engine. ADR-048 rule 3, one way per goal, names the hazard but nothing checks it.
- Recorded under the proposed flow-stop rule fbba3d5e; a predicted-stop item for the holon walk-through (f940e488).
